about.title: About me
about.text: I worked as a Cloud Support Engineer specializing in the Microsoft 365 Security and Identity ecosystem (Defender, Purview, Entra ID), and I have a backend development background in TypeScript and Node.js. Before tech, I spent years leading hospitality teams in high-pressure environments, which shaped how I handle incidents, communicate with customers and take ownership of problems.

I also spent a large part of my time organizing the company-wide materials warehouse (hundreds of references), applying organization methods and running stock control.

eventPlatform.name: Event Organization Platform
eventPlatform.problem: Staffing events: knowing how many people each shift needs, who signs up, with which specialization, and who finally works each shift — without overbooking any position.
eventPlatform.solution: Managers create events and shifts with positions per specialization (e.g. 6 waiters, 2 bartenders). Staff apply with one of their specializations; managers accept, reject or assign directly, and the system never exceeds a position's capacity. Everyone sees their own schedule and each shift's lineup. Born from my own experience running bars at large events.
highlights: Hexagonal architecture (ports & adapters): dependencies always point inward, towards the domain.
Data integrity enforced by PostgreSQL itself (composite foreign keys, partial unique indexes), not only in code.
Capacity rules checked inside the same transaction that writes (Unit of Work).
Role-based access (admin · manager · staff) with cookie-based JWT sessions.
260+ tests — unit, HTTP integration and repositories against real PostgreSQL (Testcontainers). CI also runs every migration up and down.
